ORIGINAL DERIVE NOTE: Re-derived from sonnys-corner--corner-v3.png (subject-isolated, no neighbor overrun, 4 upper floors, corner-wrap bar). Window grid = 5 columns, rows R2-R4 on all + a grilled R1 garden window at C1 only (C2/C3 ground = entrance doors, C4/C5 ground = storefront). 16 windows. Columns from not-wall density in the top row band; row y-extents from a per-row BRIGHTNESS profile down a clean column (lintel/glass/sill structure). Verified on 2x flat-texture crops. Took three passes: blob detection failed (mauve-on-mauve, dark fire escape contaminated columns); the second pass had a phantom fire-escape column + corner column ~0.045 left; the third had rows ~0.03-0.05 too HIGH (even-spacing guess, AC units included) — caught only by zooming the flat overlay to 2x. Two rules: verify window grids on HIGH-RES flat crops not 3D; vertical misalignment is never parallax (the recess normal is horizontal, so its parallax is horizontal-only). Storefront top (y0.205) and awning band (yWall 0.235 / yValance 0.18) measured by dark-fraction-per-row — the storefront is the corner half only (x0.50-1.0); the painted scalloped awning projects via the awnings component. Greenpoint face is the camera-visible frontage; the franklin return is a flat texture slice. Corner fix: the Greenpoint frontage is two collinear footprint edges (1.47m + 19.95m); sceneFrame.js now merges collinear same-role edges so the full 21.42m frontage textures as one face (was: the 1.47m corner off-cut rendered as a bare brown wall). SONNYS_KINK stays 0.734 — windows are at fixed texture-u fractions, so registration survives the merge. ALTER BROOKLYN is a SEPARATE red-brick neighbor east of the subject, correctly absent from v3.
